body: This is definitely a bug, in [`HttpClient`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/common/http/src/xhr.ts#L110), Angular already sets the `responseType` to `json`, so that browser would automatically parse the body and provide the parsed JavaScript value as `response`. Then again, [`HttpClient`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/common/http/src/xhr.ts#L182) is going to parse the already parsed result if it's a string value.

Agreed, this is a bug. Nice catch.

As a workaround, you can add an interceptor which turns the `json` request into `text` and does the `JSON.parse` itself.

[x] Bug report

## Current behavior XHRs submitted through HttpClient which return with a JSON object prefixed by `)]}',\n` are returned to the Angular application with a null body. It seems that this is because the browser tries to parse the JSON before the prefix is stripped. See [this Stack Overflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44117968/angularjs-json-vulnerability-protection-not-stripped) for reference. ## Expected behavior XHRs submitted through HttpClient should be passed through to the application. This may have to be done by changing the response type to `text` and parsing the response manually. If the user is expected to manually parse the response, this should be documented since the cause of the issue is hidden by the browser. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions Make an HttpClient.get request to an endpoint with the JSON prefix. The response body will be null. See [this plunker](http://plnkr.co/edit/CBnnX1O1jgB87oTmx7XR?p=preview) for an example. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? The prefix is to prevent [Cross-site script inclusion](https://angular.io/guide/security#xssi). This feature should be easily supported by Angular to promote security. There already is existing logic in [common/http/src/xhr.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/common/http/src/xhr.ts#L162-L166) to support the prefix but it does not work correctly. Issues #9398 and #18396 are also related. ## Environment

issue.body:
Currently HttpClient sends requests for JSON data with the
XMLHttpRequest.responseType set to 'json'. With this flag, the browser
will attempt to parse the response as JSON, but will return 'null' on
any errors. If the JSON response contains an XSSI-prevention prefix,
this will cause the browser's parsing to fail, which is unrecoverable.

The only compelling reason to use the responseType 'json' is for
performance (especially if the browser offloads JSON parsing to a
separate thread). I'm not aware of any browser which does this currently,
nor of any plans to do so. JSON.parse and responseType 'json' both
end up using the same V8 code path in Chrome to implement the parse.

Thus, this change switches all JSON parsing in HttpClient to use
JSON.parse directly.

issue.title: HttpClient throws if contentType='json' and response json encoded string
issue.body:
## I'm submitting a... [x] Bug report ## Current behavior Our API talks JSON. Everything is json encoded. And sometimes we return json encoded strings. JSON is fine with encoding/decoding strings: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/905328/31898670-ea16ddf2-b819-11e7-8e1d-92f748b7b3e3.png) But [HttpClient blindly does JSON.parse](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/common/http/src/xhr.ts#L183-L202), even if the browser already decoded it as [mentioned directly above that codeblock](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/common/http/src/xhr.ts#L181-L182). So the JSON.parse fails just like: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/905328/31898712-fa6453ec-b819-11e7-9aa1-7682387f095b.png) Here is the `HttpClient` code in the debugger: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/905328/31899120-1bcca75e-b81b-11e7-9467-4e5ff3c990a7.png) responseType is json. The response was already decoded. But HttpClient does JSON.parse anyway. Here is the same code in the debugger, if the browser returns an json encoded object: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/905328/31899394-bab4c680-b81b-11e7-9894-834b5c01ae8c.png) You see the object `{foo:"bar"}` is already a javascript object, and the only thing preventing `HttpClient` from throwing an JSON.parse error is the condition `typeof body === 'string'` ## Expected behavior Don't ever JSON.parse, if the browser already parsed it. HttpClient shouldn't throw if accepting json encoded strings. ## Environment 
Angular version: 4.3.1
